newsitem.title: USA: Senate clears new ambassadors, other posts.
newsitem.headline: Senate clears new ambassadors, other posts.

text.p: The U.S. Senate on Thursday confirmed many of the President Bill Clinton's nominations to State Department and federal posts including the new U.S. ambassadors to France, Britain and Canada.

Some of the nominees for federal judicial posts and administration positions had been waiting for Senate approval for a year. They were approved without dissent just before the Senate adjourned for its summer recess.
The U.S. envoys approved include Gordon Giffin for Canada, Felix Rohatyn for France, Philip Lader for Britain, James Collins for Russia and John Kornblum for Germany.

The Senate approved several senior State Department officials -- Karl Inderfurth, assistant secretary of state for South Asian affairs; Stanley Roth, assistant secretary of state; James Rubin, assistant secretary of state; Wendy Sherman, counsellor of the State Department; Mark Grossman, assistant secretary of state, and Bonnie Cohen, under secretary of state.

Other posts approved included James Pardew as U.S. special representative for military stabilisation in the Balkans; Peter Burleigh, deputy U.S. representative to the United Nations; David Scheffer, ambassador at large for war crimes issues, and Richard Sklar, U.S. representative to the United Nations for U.N. management and reform.
